plan: Store the workspace as a deep-copied dict tree; items keep their original dict shape so to_data() is just another deep copy.
Implement each query (total_word_count, unresolved_markers, outline) as one recursive traversal dispatching on item kind, so notes/references/containers are handled uniformly at every depth.

Count note words by replacing each [[?identifier]] marker with a space, then counting \b\w+\b runs, so marker syntax and identifiers never count but adjacent words stay separate; references contribute their declared word_count.
Collect markers from note text via regex and from reference 'unresolved' lists into a set, returned sorted for determinism.
Render the outline with a preorder walk: workspace title at column 0, each item indented two spaces per nesting level (top-level items at level 1) as '<kind>: <title>'.

For move(), locate the item and destination first, then run all validations (string ids, existence, destination is workspace/section/group, index within 0..len(dest), destination not the item itself or inside its subtree) before any mutation, guaranteeing failed moves leave the tree untouched.
Perform the move as pop-from-parent then append/insert into destination, reusing the same node object so the item and its descendants are preserved exactly.
mechanisms: recursive part-whole tree of section/group containers over note/reference leaves
uniform kind-dispatched operations applied at every nesting level
recursive aggregation for total word count
deterministic preorder traversal for outline and sorted-set collection for markers
containment invariant enforced by subtree-membership and container-kind checks
atomic move via full validation before any mutation
